findings.title: Snapshot projection changes beyond the PRD B/C adapter deliverables
findings.detail: projectSnapshot now ignores non-status events when picking a node's last event and maps a new 'interrupted' event status to paused. Both are reasonable (a trailing 'stopped' note no longer masks the last status; an interrupted native review is unresolved, not pending) and tested, but neither is listed in the PRD adapter deliverables or the contract README's state-projection rules, and the first alters projection for existing runs whose last recorded event is a 'stopped' record.
findings.evidence: server/projects.ts:239 `interrupted: 'paused'`; :842 `if (EVENT_STATUS[event.status] !== undefined) lastEvent.set(node, event)` (main: `lastEvent.set(node, event)` unconditionally); test server/projects.test.ts:1241-1262. Live events.jsonl statuses include `stopped` (probe: `['approved','blocked','interactive','passed','running','stopped','succeeded']`).

findings.title: Deviates from PRD C wording (inputs: null) in favour of 404 INPUTS_NOT_FOUND, documented
findings.detail: PRD_RUN_INPUTS section 5 asks the adapter for 'inputs: null for runs without the section' and 'a verbatim match flag per finding'. PR 11 returns 404 INPUTS_NOT_FOUND and an array requirement_found_in of lanes instead. Both are defensible (the 404 keeps the payload strict and the UI maps the code to 'not recorded'; lanes handle worker=both without a second field) and the contract README records the 404 convention, but it is a deviation from the PRD's literal deliverable that PR 10's spec follows.
findings.evidence: docs/PRD_RUN_INPUTS.md (main) section 5: "`inputs: null` for runs without the section; requirement-quote lookup exposed as a verbatim match flag per finding"; server/projects.ts:603 `if (!run.inputs) throw new ProjectApiError(404, 'INPUTS_NOT_FOUND', ...)`; contracts/projects/README.md (PR 11) "A run whose export predates a section returns a 404 with code `REVIEW_NOT_FOUND` or `INPUTS_NOT_FOUND`"; features/run-inputs/adapter-task.md (PR 10):42 "`{ \"inputs\": RunInputs | null }` ... `null` when the section is absent or null".

findings.title: Adapter-task verification list is concrete and names the negative paths
findings.detail: The B task's verification paragraph enumerates exactly the cases a security-minded reviewer would want: all three export versions load, three transports, findings with and without worker/requirement, blocked review, attempt 2 and missing review are 404, diff confinement/symlink/hash-mismatch/oversize failures, redaction in messages and quotes, and existing tests passing without project configuration. It also fixes the version-acceptance rule (major 1, minor >= 0), pins ownership to server/ and config/projects.example.json, and carries the honesty clause about not claiming unexecuted tests. The C task adds truncation-marker passthrough and the true/false/null matrix for requirement_verbatim including both and none.
findings.evidence: features/review-result/adapter-task.md (PR 10):21 "export versions 1.0.0, 1.1.0 and 1.2.0 all load; a review section with native, print and manual transports; ... attempt 2 and missing review are 404; ... the diff artifact's confinement, symlink, hash-mismatch and oversize failures; path redaction in messages and quotes"; features/run-inputs/adapter-task.md (PR 10):49 "`requirement_verbatim` true, false and null cases including `both` and `none`, and the null case when inputs are missing; unknown run is 404".

findings.title: Spec leaves load-bearing choices open that the UI worker and seeds depend on
findings.detail: The B task says the artifact_id is 'of your choice', the content type is 'text/x-diff or text/plain', and the missing-review 404 uses 'a code that says no review is recorded' without naming it. The UI worker runs in parallel against the same spec and must mock the reviews route, seed candidate-mode runs and branch on the 404 code, so two workers could ship non-interlocking choices (e.g. UI expects REVIEW_NOT_FOUND, adapter emits NO_REVIEW). Compare PR 11's adapter task, which fixes `patch-review-<sha12>`, `text/plain; charset=utf-8`, `REVIEW_NOT_FOUND`, `INPUTS_NOT_FOUND` and the exact truncation marker.
findings.evidence: features/review-result/adapter-task.md (PR 10):12 "a run without a review section is 404 with a code that says no review is recorded"; :14 "(`artifact_id` of your choice, content type `text/x-diff` or `text/plain`, ...)". PR 11 features/review-result/adapter-task.md:12 "404 `REVIEW_NOT_FOUND` when the run has no review section or the attempt is not the recorded one"; :14 "artifact id `patch-review-<first 12 hex of sha256>` ... served `text/plain; charset=utf-8` inline".

findings.title: diff_artifact null-on-check-failure forces a full diff read on every reviews request and hides tampering
findings.detail: The spec requires diff_artifact to be null 'when the export has no diff or the file fails its checks (the reviews route still succeeds)'. To know whether the file fails its checks the reviews route must open, bound-read (up to 32 MiB) and hash review.diff on every call, and a hash mismatch or symlink is then reported as 'no diff' rather than as evidence tampering. The live run's review.diff is 289 KB, so the cost is real but bounded; the bigger issue is that a security signal (ARTIFACT_HASH_MISMATCH) is downgraded to an absence. PR 11 instead links by registry and lets the artifact route fail loudly (test 'tampered' asserts the link is present and the artifact route returns ARTIFACT_HASH_MISMATCH).
findings.evidence: features/review-result/adapter-task.md (PR 10):14 "`diff_artifact` is `null` when the export has no diff or the file fails its checks (the reviews route still succeeds)". Live run: `-rw-rw-r-- 1 agentops agentops 289187 Sep 21 15:36 review.diff`. PR 11 server/projects.test.ts:1019-1021 `const tampered = validateReviewResult(...); assert.equal(tampered.diff!.artifact_id, \`patch-review-${'e'.repeat(12)}\`)` with :1009 `assertError(await artifact('tampered', ...), 500, 'ARTIFACT_HASH_MISMATCH', root)`.

findings.title: Contract feeding the spec has enum and pattern gaps a faithful worker would inherit
findings.detail: PR 10's runInputs contract allows checks[].kind of only build/unit/browser/contract while the committed policy schema allows six kinds (typecheck, integration too); check and scenario ids use the 128-char route-ID pattern, which rejects free-form policy labels (e.g. test:unit, 'review verdict / narrow'); mode is z.enum(['interactive']) (a single-value enum copied from plan.mode); source_branch is non-nullable and export_inputs returns None when the plan lacks it, so such runs get inputs: null with no way to show even the task text. A worker implementing the spec against this contract would make the inputs route a 500 RESPONSE_INVALID for any policy using the other two kinds or a colon in a check id. PR 11's contract matches the six kinds and accepts free-form labels (tested).
findings.evidence: contracts/projects/v1.ts (PR 10) `kind: z.enum(['build', 'unit', 'browser', 'contract'])`, `id: id`, `scenarios: z.array(z.strictObject({ id: id, ... }))`, `mode: z.enum(['interactive'])`, `source_branch: z.string().min(1)`; workflow/export_state.py (PR 10) `if policy is None or "source_branch" not in plan: return None`. Probe on main: contracts/workflow/verification.schema.json enums -> `['build','typecheck','unit','integration','contract','browser']`, check id `{'type': 'string', 'minLength': 1}`. PR 11 contracts/projects/contract.test.ts `older.workers[0].checks[0].id = 'test:unit'` validates.

findings.title: requirement_verbatim compares redacted quote to redacted task, which can false-link a literal <path> quote
findings.detail: The C task says the flag is true 'when the redacted quote is a verbatim substring of the redacted task text'. A reviewer who writes the quote with the marker '<path>' (copying it from the viewer) would then match any task that contains a redacted absolute path at that position, which is a small guess by construction. PR 11 matches raw against raw and only then checks the redacted quote survives in the served text, and tests the '<path>'-literal case yields no link.
findings.evidence: features/run-inputs/adapter-task.md (PR 10):44 "`true` when the redacted quote is a verbatim substring of the redacted task text of the named worker"; features/run-inputs/README.md (PR 10) "the verbatim lookup compares redacted quote to redacted task". PR 11 server/projects.test.ts:943 `finding({ message: 'A redacted spelling is not the raw text.', worker: 'ui', requirement: 'Write the harness to <path> before anything else.' })` -> `[]`.

findings.title: Export bumped to 1.2.0 while the shipped adapter still requires exactly 1.0.0
findings.detail: PR 10 changes EXPORT_VERSION to '1.2.0' in workflow/export_state.py but does not touch server/projects.ts, where exportSchema.version is z.literal('1.0.0'). Every run recorded after PR 10 merges is RUN_STORAGE_INVALID in the viewer, and because listRuns projects every run, one such run makes the whole workflow list a 500 until slice B's feature run lands its adapter. The handoff discloses this honestly and defers `workflow export` on the live run for the same reason, but it is a self-inflicted interim breakage from shipping the producer bump ahead of the consumer; keeping the producer at 1.0.0 (as PR 9 does) or landing the two-line version-acceptance change (as PR 11 does) would have avoided it.
findings.evidence: workflow/export_state.py (PR 10) `EXPORT_VERSION = "1.2.0"` and `value = {"version": EXPORT_VERSION, ...}`; server/projects.ts on main :37 `const EXPORT_VERSION = '1.0.0'` / :52 `version: z.literal(EXPORT_VERSION)` (unchanged in PR 10: `git diff 61e4752..a1fab98 --stat` lists no server/ file); docs/HANDOFF_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md (PR 10):76-77 "the adapter on `main` accepts export version 1.0.0 only, so re-exporting the live run before slice B's adapter merges would break the viewer ... new runs export at version 1.2.0, which the current adapter rejects for that run's listing".

findings.title: Spec is silent on malformed review/inputs sections
findings.detail: Neither PR 10 adapter task says what the adapter does when the review or inputs section is present but fails validation (500 for the run only, 500 for the workflow list, or serve the run without the section). Given main's eager-projection pattern this is the highest-blast-radius decision the worker will make, and PR 11's task states it explicitly ('RUN_STORAGE_INVALID naming the run but never a path') and tests it.
findings.evidence: features/review-result/adapter-task.md (PR 10):11-17 covers absent/null sections and unknown top-level keys only; PR 11 features/review-result/adapter-task.md:11 "A violation is `RUN_STORAGE_INVALID` naming the run but never a path. Never trust `values.review`."

findings.title: No adapter work, and none needed: producer left at 1.0.0 so the viewer is unaffected
findings.detail: PR 9 confines itself to slice A and leaves workflow/export_state.py at version 1.0.0, so main's z.literal('1.0.0') adapter keeps loading every new run and the live project-workflows-001 export continues to validate. There is nothing to review on this dimension and nothing misleading about that; it is the restraint the umbrella PRD asked for.

I probed the old and new redactPaths regexes on edge-case strings and zod's timestamp/error-message behaviour in the scratchpad, and inspected the live project-workflows-001 run's receipts to confirm the adapter's normalisations match real files. PR 11 is the only PR with adapter code and it is careful, security-minded work that matches the existing adapter's conventions: strict section schemas, a materially better redaction regex, a hash-and-size-checked review.diff artifact reusing the no-follow bounded reader, verbatim-only requirement lookup with a served-text guard, 404-not-500 for absent sections, and a test file whose negative-path matrix is stronger than main's. Its diff_artifact rule ("null when the file fails its checks, the reviews route still succeeds") forces the reviews route to open, bound-read and hash up to 32 MiB on every request and silently downgrades tampering to null. The C task's requirement_verbatim compares redacted quote to redacted task, which can false-link a literal "<path>" quote. The contract feeding the spec has gaps a faithful worker would inherit: checks[].kind omits typecheck/integration (policy schema allows six), check/scenario id use the route-ID pattern (rejects labels like test:unit), mode is z.enum(['interactive']), source_branch is required so runs without it get inputs:null. It says nothing about what happens when a review/inputs section is malformed. Meanwhile PR 10 bumps EXPORT_VERSION to "1.2.0" while main's adapter is z.literal('1.0.0'): every run recorded after merging PR 10 is RUN_STORAGE_INVALID in the viewer until B's feature run merges; disclosed at docs/HANDOFF_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md:76-77 but self-inflicted by shipping the producer bump before the consumer. Two workers given this spec would produce broadly equivalent but not interchangeable code.
toolu_01YGBqZJCy5azK7jzWQ7EmV2.pr11: Shipped adapter code of high quality, consistent with main's style (ProjectApiError codes, readBounded/openDirectory/withRunsRoot reuse, JSDoc one-liners, routes registered via the paths map so the 405 loop and HEAD cover them). Export acceptance is an explicit enum of 1.0.0/1.1.0/1.2.0 (server/projects.ts:44) with review/inputs optional-or-null and strictly validated (:73-90, :123-142), and values.review is never mined. Redaction is materially improved (:57): my probe shows main leaves "[/home/u/x]", "|/home/u/x|", "<~/x/y>", "*~/a/b*" and "file:///home/..." unredacted while PR 11 redacts all of them, with no regression on URLs, relative paths or "2/3". review.diff is registered only under the literal path "review.diff" (:89), served via the existing artifact route with the same no-follow bounded read, an added size check (:651), text/plain + nosniff + CSP sandbox, and the test fixture deliberately embeds "<script>alert(1)</script>". requirement_found_in matches raw quote against raw task/prompt and additionally requires the redacted quote to survive in the served (64 KiB-bounded) text (:397-406); nothing is inferred. Absent sections are 404 REVIEW_NOT_FOUND/INPUTS_NOT_FOUND (:592-605), malformed ones are RUN_STORAGE_INVALID naming only the run. Tests (30, up from 22) assert no root path and no /home|/tmp|/var in every error body, snapshot the run tree to prove reads never write, cover 405/HEAD on the new routes and a 22-case malformed-section matrix. Weaknesses are modest: exact-version enum plus eager section validation means one 1.3.0 or one bad receipt field in one run makes the whole workflow list 500 (pre-existing pattern, larger surface now); checks[].command and setup[].command pass through unredacted by design; validateReviewResult runs three times per review request; native_started_at above 8.64e15 ms throws RangeError into the generic 500 path; the feature README still says "not an implementation" while the same PR ships it. Its own adapter-task.md matches the shipped code line for line and is precise enough to reproduce it.
toolu_01YGBqZJCy5azK7jzWQ7EmV2.ranking_reason: PR 11 is the only PR with adapter code and the code is careful, well-tested and stylistically consistent with main; on the security points that matter here (redaction, artifact registry checks, bounded reads, path-free errors, never guessing a match) it is verifiably better than what main has today. PR 10's specification is competent and its verification list is good, but it leaves load-bearing details open, prescribes a heavier diff_artifact design, inherits contract gaps, and ships an export bump that breaks the viewer for new runs until the future adapter lands. PR 9 has nothing on this dimension, which is correct for slice A, so it ranks last by definition rather than by fault.

findings.title: Redaction regex genuinely closes Markdown-punctuation and file:// gaps
findings.detail: PR 11 replaces main's lookbehind allow-list with a negative lookbehind on path characters plus an explicit file:// branch. A scratch probe shows main leaves paths inside [], ||, <>, ** and file:/// unredacted while PR 11 redacts all of them, and neither regex touches https URLs, relative paths, './x', '../x' or '2/3'. The test at server/projects.test.ts:1197 pins every spelling.
findings.evidence: server/projects.ts:57 `text.replace(/(?:file:\/\/(?=\/)|(?<![A-Za-z0-9._@~+/-]))(?:~|\/[A-Za-z0-9._@~+-]+)(?:\/[A-Za-z0-9._@~+-]*)+/g, '<path>')`. Probe (node redact.mjs): input `see [/home/u/x](/home/u/x) and |/home/u/x| and <~/x/y> *~/a/b*` -> main: `see [/home/u/x](<path>) and |/home/u/x| and <~/x/y> *~/a/b*`; ultra: `see [<path>](<path>) and |<path>| and <<path>> *<path>*`. `file:///home/u/repo/x.ts` -> main unchanged, ultra `<path>`. `https://example.com/a/b`, `src/projects/api.ts`, `../up/x`, `2/3` unchanged in both.

findings.title: review.diff artifact registration is pinned, hash-and-size checked and served with safe headers
findings.detail: The export's diff registration only validates with path literally 'review.diff' (traversal is rejected at schema level, tests review-diff-path / review-diff-traversal), the artifact id is derived from the registered hash, the file is read through the existing no-follow bounded reader under artifactByteLimit, and the served bytes must match both registered sha256 and byte count. Content type is text/plain with nosniff and CSP sandbox; the fixture embeds a script tag to prove it is inert. Untrusted packets do not block the review diff and a tampered registration surfaces as ARTIFACT_HASH_MISMATCH rather than a silently null link.
findings.evidence: server/projects.ts:89 `diff: z.strictObject({ path: z.literal(REVIEW_DIFF_FILE), sha256: hex64, bytes: ... })`; :617 `registered.push({ components: [REVIEW_DIFF_FILE], kind: 'patch', ... bytes: run.reviewDiff.bytes })`; :651 `if ((artifact.bytes !== null && bytes.length !== artifact.bytes) || sha256(bytes) !== artifact.sha256)`. Test server/projects.test.ts:979-1024 covers served/tampered/shorter/missing/symlinked-outside/oversize/none with `assert.equal(served.headers['content-type'], 'text/plain; charset=utf-8')`, nosniff, `default-src 'none'; sandbox`, and `assert.ok(!linked.body.includes('top secret'))`.

findings.title: requirement_found_in never guesses and is guarded against the served-text cut
findings.detail: A lane is linked only when the raw quote is a substring of the raw task (or prompt when the task is empty) AND the redacted quote survives in the bounded served text, so a link can never point at text the viewer cannot show. A quote written with the literal '<path>' marker does not match raw text; a paraphrase does not match; a null requirement yields []. The contract's cross-field validator additionally rejects links without a quote and duplicate lanes.
findings.evidence: server/projects.ts:397-406 `return text.includes(requirement) && boundedText(text).text.includes(served)`. Tests: server/projects.test.ts:932-960 asserts `requirement_found_in` = `[['ui'], [], [], ['ui'], [], ['adapter'], []]` for verbatim / paraphrase / none / path-in-quote / '<path>'-literal / both / legacy-null; :1197-1234 asserts a quote verbatim in the raw task but past the 64 KiB cut yields `[]`.

findings.title: Test file is stronger than main's on negative paths and leak checks
findings.detail: Every error assertion routes through assertError, which checks the body shape, that the temp root never appears, and that the message matches no /home|/tmp|/var path. The read-only test snapshots the run tree before and after hitting all routes including the new ones, checks 405+Allow for five methods and HEAD 200. The malformed-section test enumerates 22 mutations (unknown version, wrong types, extra keys carrying absolute paths, absolute/traversal owned_paths, foreign lane, duplicate check ids, browser without scenarios, unconfirmed stop with a time) and asserts the run list names only the run directory. Fixtures mirror real receipts (offset +00:00 timestamps, epoch-ms native_started_at) as found in the live run's ui.interactive.json.

findings.title: Adapter code follows main's conventions and its adapter-task.md matches the shipped code
findings.detail: New routes are added to the paths map so the existing 405 loop and Fastify HEAD handling cover them; conform() is reused; errors are ProjectApiError with upper-snake codes; invalidRun() redacts issue text; helper functions carry the same one-line JSDoc style. PR 11's features/*/adapter-task.md names the exact version set, route, error codes, artifact id format, content type, headers, truncation limit and marker string, timestamp normalisation and launch_node_id rule, and each item corresponds to shipped code.

findings.title: Exact-version enum plus eager section validation lets one run poison the whole workflow list
findings.detail: exportSchema.version is z.enum(['1.0.0','1.1.0','1.2.0']) and review/inputs are projected eagerly inside projectRun, which listRuns calls for every run. One run exported at 1.2.1/1.3.0, or one receipt field the strict section schema rejects (e.g. a policy check kind outside the enum, a non-UTC timestamp string, an unexpected key), makes GET .../runs a 500 for the entire workflow. This is main's pre-existing pattern for the core export, but the validated surface grew from about a dozen fields to roughly sixty optional-receipt fields. PR 10's spec asks for 'major 1 and minor >= 0', which is more forward-compatible. The test explicitly pins the whole-list failure.
findings.evidence: server/projects.ts:44 `const EXPORT_VERSIONS = ['1.0.0', '1.1.0', '1.2.0'] as const`; :693 `// Sections are projected eagerly so a contradictory review or assignment fails the run as a whole`; server/projects.test.ts:1163 case `{ ...base, runId: 'unknown-version', version: '1.3.0', ... }` and :1187-1188 `const list = await get(app, url('alpha', 'main')); assertError(list, 500, 'RUN_STORAGE_INVALID', root)`. Contrast features/review-result/adapter-task.md (PR 10):11 "Accept run-state.json exports whose version has major 1 and minor >= 0 (1.0.0, 1.1.0, 1.2.0, later 1.2.x)".

findings.title: checks[].command and setup[].command are served unredacted by design
findings.detail: Task, prompt, summaries, assumptions, finding messages and quotes all pass through redactPaths, but the joined argv commands do not, so an absolute interpreter or config path in a committed policy.json would reach the client. This is deliberate (the contract says command must equal the verifier's recorded command so a required check links to its execution) and consistent with main's projectWorkerResult, which also passes check commands through unredacted; the current policies contain no absolute paths. Worth a README note that policy commands are treated as operator-public.
findings.evidence: server/projects.ts:441 `id: check.id, kind: check.kind, command: check.command, ...`; :456 `setup: section.setup.map(step => ({ command: step.command, timeout_seconds: step.timeout_seconds }))`; contracts/projects/v1.ts (PR 11) "The approved argv joined exactly as the verifier records executed commands, so check IDs can be matched to executed checks". Probe: `python3 -c ... re.findall(r'"(/[^"]*)"', json.dumps(policy))` on the live policy.json -> `[]`.

findings.title: Oversized native_started_at reaches the generic 500 path instead of RUN_STORAGE_INVALID
findings.detail: The section schema accepts any non-negative integer for native_started_at, but new Date(n).toISOString() throws RangeError for n > 8.64e15, which escapes projectInputs, is not a ProjectApiError, and becomes 500 INTERNAL via the scope error handler. No path leaks (the message is fixed), so this is a wrong-code nit, not a security issue; a .max(8.64e15) on the schema or a try/catch would make it RUN_STORAGE_INVALID like every other malformed field.
findings.evidence: server/projects.ts:446 `native_started_at: worker.launch.native_started_at === null ? null : new Date(worker.launch.native_started_at).toISOString()`; :112 `native_started_at: z.number().int().nonnegative().nullable()`. Probe: `try { new Date(1e20).toISOString() } catch (e) { ... }` -> `big epoch -> RangeError Invalid time value`.

findings.title: Review payload is validated three times per request and redaction is recomputed per lane per finding
findings.detail: projectRun already calls validateReviewResult (and validateRunInputs) when loading the run; the route then wraps the same object in crossChecked(validateReviewResult) and conform(schemas.reviewResult). Harmless but redundant. Separately, lanesQuoting calls boundedText(text) (a full redaction pass over up to 256 KiB of task text) for each finding x lane, and because sections are projected eagerly this runs for every run on every list request. Bounded and small today, but it compounds the existing per-request packet loading the live reviewer already flagged.
findings.evidence: server/projects.ts:696-706 `inputs = validateRunInputs(projectInputs(...))` / `review = validateReviewResult(projectReview(...))`; server/projectRoutes.ts:167-174 `conform(schemas.reviewResult, crossChecked(() => validateReviewResult(review), log), log)`; server/projects.ts:400-405 `return WORKER_LANES.filter(lane => { ... return text.includes(requirement) && boundedText(text).text.includes(served) })`.

findings.title: Feature READMEs still describe the adapter as future worker work that the same PR ships
findings.detail: features/review-result/README.md and features/run-inputs/README.md say the directory is 'the committed assignment for the two workers ... not an implementation' and the adapter tasks open with 'Implement the backend side of slice B/C', while server/ in the same commit contains the implementation. The PRD status lines do record that the slices were implemented directly and that the feature directories 'exist for a later run', so this is stale wording rather than a misleading claim, but a worker launched from these tasks would re-implement shipped routes.
findings.evidence: features/review-result/README.md:3 "This directory is the committed assignment for the two workers of `docs/PRD_REVIEW_RESULT.md`, **not** an implementation."; features/review-result/adapter-task.md:3 "Implement the backend side of slice B ... on the existing Fastify server."; docs/PRD_REVIEW_RESULT.md (PR 11) "Status: Implemented 2026-09-21 on branch `ultra` directly in the checkout rather than as a feature run ...; the `review-result` feature directory and launch choice exist for a later run."; server/projects.ts:592 `async reviewResult(...)` shipped.

findings.title: Snapshot projection changes beyond the PRD B/C adapter deliverables
findings.detail: projectSnapshot now ignores non-status events when picking a node's last event and maps a new 'interrupted' event status to paused. Both are reasonable (a trailing 'stopped' note no longer masks the last status; an interrupted native review is unresolved, not pending) and tested, but neither is listed in the PRD adapter deliverables or the contract README's state-projection rules, and the first alters projection for existing runs whose last recorded event is a 'stopped' record.
findings.evidence: server/projects.ts:239 `interrupted: 'paused'`; :842 `if (EVENT_STATUS[event.status] !== undefined) lastEvent.set(node, event)` (main: `lastEvent.set(node, event)` unconditionally); test server/projects.test.ts:1241-1262. Live events.jsonl statuses include `stopped` (probe: `['approved','blocked','interactive','passed','running','stopped','succeeded']`).

findings.title: Deviates from PRD C wording (inputs: null) in favour of 404 INPUTS_NOT_FOUND, documented
findings.detail: PRD_RUN_INPUTS section 5 asks the adapter for 'inputs: null for runs without the section' and 'a verbatim match flag per finding'. PR 11 returns 404 INPUTS_NOT_FOUND and an array requirement_found_in of lanes instead. Both are defensible (the 404 keeps the payload strict and the UI maps the code to 'not recorded'; lanes handle worker=both without a second field) and the contract README records the 404 convention, but it is a deviation from the PRD's literal deliverable that PR 10's spec follows.
findings.evidence: docs/PRD_RUN_INPUTS.md (main) section 5: "`inputs: null` for runs without the section; requirement-quote lookup exposed as a verbatim match flag per finding"; server/projects.ts:603 `if (!run.inputs) throw new ProjectApiError(404, 'INPUTS_NOT_FOUND', ...)`; contracts/projects/README.md (PR 11) "A run whose export predates a section returns a 404 with code `REVIEW_NOT_FOUND` or `INPUTS_NOT_FOUND`"; features/run-inputs/adapter-task.md (PR 10):42 "`{ \"inputs\": RunInputs | null }` ... `null` when the section is absent or null".

findings.title: Adapter-task verification list is concrete and names the negative paths
findings.detail: The B task's verification paragraph enumerates exactly the cases a security-minded reviewer would want: all three export versions load, three transports, findings with and without worker/requirement, blocked review, attempt 2 and missing review are 404, diff confinement/symlink/hash-mismatch/oversize failures, redaction in messages and quotes, and existing tests passing without project configuration. It also fixes the version-acceptance rule (major 1, minor >= 0), pins ownership to server/ and config/projects.example.json, and carries the honesty clause about not claiming unexecuted tests. The C task adds truncation-marker passthrough and the true/false/null matrix for requirement_verbatim including both and none.
findings.evidence: features/review-result/adapter-task.md (PR 10):21 "export versions 1.0.0, 1.1.0 and 1.2.0 all load; a review section with native, print and manual transports; ... attempt 2 and missing review are 404; ... the diff artifact's confinement, symlink, hash-mismatch and oversize failures; path redaction in messages and quotes"; features/run-inputs/adapter-task.md (PR 10):49 "`requirement_verbatim` true, false and null cases including `both` and `none`, and the null case when inputs are missing; unknown run is 404".

findings.title: Spec leaves load-bearing choices open that the UI worker and seeds depend on
findings.detail: The B task says the artifact_id is 'of your choice', the content type is 'text/x-diff or text/plain', and the missing-review 404 uses 'a code that says no review is recorded' without naming it. The UI worker runs in parallel against the same spec and must mock the reviews route, seed candidate-mode runs and branch on the 404 code, so two workers could ship non-interlocking choices (e.g. UI expects REVIEW_NOT_FOUND, adapter emits NO_REVIEW). Compare PR 11's adapter task, which fixes `patch-review-<sha12>`, `text/plain; charset=utf-8`, `REVIEW_NOT_FOUND`, `INPUTS_NOT_FOUND` and the exact truncation marker.
findings.evidence: features/review-result/adapter-task.md (PR 10):12 "a run without a review section is 404 with a code that says no review is recorded"; :14 "(`artifact_id` of your choice, content type `text/x-diff` or `text/plain`, ...)". PR 11 features/review-result/adapter-task.md:12 "404 `REVIEW_NOT_FOUND` when the run has no review section or the attempt is not the recorded one"; :14 "artifact id `patch-review-<first 12 hex of sha256>` ... served `text/plain; charset=utf-8` inline".

findings.title: diff_artifact null-on-check-failure forces a full diff read on every reviews request and hides tampering
findings.detail: The spec requires diff_artifact to be null 'when the export has no diff or the file fails its checks (the reviews route still succeeds)'. To know whether the file fails its checks the reviews route must open, bound-read (up to 32 MiB) and hash review.diff on every call, and a hash mismatch or symlink is then reported as 'no diff' rather than as evidence tampering. The live run's review.diff is 289 KB, so the cost is real but bounded; the bigger issue is that a security signal (ARTIFACT_HASH_MISMATCH) is downgraded to an absence. PR 11 instead links by registry and lets the artifact route fail loudly (test 'tampered' asserts the link is present and the artifact route returns ARTIFACT_HASH_MISMATCH).
findings.evidence: features/review-result/adapter-task.md (PR 10):14 "`diff_artifact` is `null` when the export has no diff or the file fails its checks (the reviews route still succeeds)". Live run: `-rw-rw-r-- 1 agentops agentops 289187 Sep 21 15:36 review.diff`. PR 11 server/projects.test.ts:1019-1021 `const tampered = validateReviewResult(...); assert.equal(tampered.diff!.artifact_id, \`patch-review-${'e'.repeat(12)}\`)` with :1009 `assertError(await artifact('tampered', ...), 500, 'ARTIFACT_HASH_MISMATCH', root)`.

findings.title: Contract feeding the spec has enum and pattern gaps a faithful worker would inherit
findings.detail: PR 10's runInputs contract allows checks[].kind of only build/unit/browser/contract while the committed policy schema allows six kinds (typecheck, integration too); check and scenario ids use the 128-char route-ID pattern, which rejects free-form policy labels (e.g. test:unit, 'review verdict / narrow'); mode is z.enum(['interactive']) (a single-value enum copied from plan.mode); source_branch is non-nullable and export_inputs returns None when the plan lacks it, so such runs get inputs: null with no way to show even the task text. A worker implementing the spec against this contract would make the inputs route a 500 RESPONSE_INVALID for any policy using the other two kinds or a colon in a check id. PR 11's contract matches the six kinds and accepts free-form labels (tested).
findings.evidence: contracts/projects/v1.ts (PR 10) `kind: z.enum(['build', 'unit', 'browser', 'contract'])`, `id: id`, `scenarios: z.array(z.strictObject({ id: id, ... }))`, `mode: z.enum(['interactive'])`, `source_branch: z.string().min(1)`; workflow/export_state.py (PR 10) `if policy is None or "source_branch" not in plan: return None`. Probe on main: contracts/workflow/verification.schema.json enums -> `['build','typecheck','unit','integration','contract','browser']`, check id `{'type': 'string', 'minLength': 1}`. PR 11 contracts/projects/contract.test.ts `older.workers[0].checks[0].id = 'test:unit'` validates.

findings.title: requirement_verbatim compares redacted quote to redacted task, which can false-link a literal <path> quote
findings.detail: The C task says the flag is true 'when the redacted quote is a verbatim substring of the redacted task text'. A reviewer who writes the quote with the marker '<path>' (copying it from the viewer) would then match any task that contains a redacted absolute path at that position, which is a small guess by construction. PR 11 matches raw against raw and only then checks the redacted quote survives in the served text, and tests the '<path>'-literal case yields no link.
findings.evidence: features/run-inputs/adapter-task.md (PR 10):44 "`true` when the redacted quote is a verbatim substring of the redacted task text of the named worker"; features/run-inputs/README.md (PR 10) "the verbatim lookup compares redacted quote to redacted task". PR 11 server/projects.test.ts:943 `finding({ message: 'A redacted spelling is not the raw text.', worker: 'ui', requirement: 'Write the harness to <path> before anything else.' })` -> `[]`.

findings.title: Export bumped to 1.2.0 while the shipped adapter still requires exactly 1.0.0
findings.detail: PR 10 changes EXPORT_VERSION to '1.2.0' in workflow/export_state.py but does not touch server/projects.ts, where exportSchema.version is z.literal('1.0.0'). Every run recorded after PR 10 merges is RUN_STORAGE_INVALID in the viewer, and because listRuns projects every run, one such run makes the whole workflow list a 500 until slice B's feature run lands its adapter. The handoff discloses this honestly and defers `workflow export` on the live run for the same reason, but it is a self-inflicted interim breakage from shipping the producer bump ahead of the consumer; keeping the producer at 1.0.0 (as PR 9 does) or landing the two-line version-acceptance change (as PR 11 does) would have avoided it.
findings.evidence: workflow/export_state.py (PR 10) `EXPORT_VERSION = "1.2.0"` and `value = {"version": EXPORT_VERSION, ...}`; server/projects.ts on main :37 `const EXPORT_VERSION = '1.0.0'` / :52 `version: z.literal(EXPORT_VERSION)` (unchanged in PR 10: `git diff 61e4752..a1fab98 --stat` lists no server/ file); docs/HANDOFF_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md (PR 10):76-77 "the adapter on `main` accepts export version 1.0.0 only, so re-exporting the live run before slice B's adapter merges would break the viewer ... new runs export at version 1.2.0, which the current adapter rejects for that run's listing".

findings.title: Spec is silent on malformed review/inputs sections
findings.detail: Neither PR 10 adapter task says what the adapter does when the review or inputs section is present but fails validation (500 for the run only, 500 for the workflow list, or serve the run without the section). Given main's eager-projection pattern this is the highest-blast-radius decision the worker will make, and PR 11's task states it explicitly ('RUN_STORAGE_INVALID naming the run but never a path') and tests it.
findings.evidence: features/review-result/adapter-task.md (PR 10):11-17 covers absent/null sections and unknown top-level keys only; PR 11 features/review-result/adapter-task.md:11 "A violation is `RUN_STORAGE_INVALID` naming the run but never a path. Never trust `values.review`."

findings.title: No adapter work, and none needed: producer left at 1.0.0 so the viewer is unaffected
findings.detail: PR 9 confines itself to slice A and leaves workflow/export_state.py at version 1.0.0, so main's z.literal('1.0.0') adapter keeps loading every new run and the live project-workflows-001 export continues to validate. There is nothing to review on this dimension and nothing misleading about that; it is the restraint the umbrella PRD asked for.
findings.evidence: pr9.diff touches no server/ or workflow/export_state.py file (task-stated file set: 21 files, slice A only); server/projects.ts on main :37 `const EXPORT_VERSION = '1.0.0'`; ~/.local/state/md-manager-workflows/project-workflows/project-workflows-001/run-state.json `version` = `1.0.0` (probe output `1.0.0 2026-09-21T14:33:23.528543Z 2026-09-21T15:52:04.675731Z`).

data.summary: I read main's server/projects.ts and projectRoutes.ts as the style baseline, PR 11's full server/ diff (projects.ts +305, projectRoutes.ts +29, projects.test.ts +446), its contracts/projects/v1.ts and export_state.py to check producer/adapter shape agreement, and the two adapter-task.md specs (PR 10 and PR 11) against PRD_REVIEW_RESULT.md / PRD_RUN_INPUTS.md. I probed the old and new redactPaths regexes on edge-case strings and zod's timestamp/error-message behaviour in the scratchpad, and inspected the live project-workflows-001 run's receipts to confirm the adapter's normalisations match real files. PR 11 is the only PR with adapter code and it is careful, security-minded work that matches the existing adapter's conventions: strict section schemas, a materially better redaction regex, a hash-and-size-checked review.diff artifact reusing the no-follow bounded reader, verbatim-only requirement lookup with a served-text guard, 404-not-500 for absent sections, and a test file whose negative-path matrix is stronger than main's. PR 10's adapter-task.md is a competent specification with a detailed verification list but leaves load-bearing choices open (artifact id, content type, 404 code), imposes a costly design for diff_artifact, and its contract carries enum/pattern gaps a faithful worker would inherit; its own export bump to 1.2.0 against an adapter still pinned to 1.0.0 leaves new runs unviewable until the feature run merges. PR 9 ships nothing on this dimension and correctly needed nothing.
data.pr9: Not applicable: no server/ change and none required by slice A. The one thing worth crediting is restraint, and it is real: PR 9 leaves export_state at 1.0.0, so the adapter on main keeps validating every new run (z.literal('1.0.0') in server/projects.ts:37 on main) and the existing live run keeps loading. It neither describes nor implies adapter work. Scored 0 per instructions.
data.pr10: Specification only (features/review-result/adapter-task.md, features/run-inputs/adapter-task.md), no adapter code. The B task is precise on ownership, version acceptance ("major 1 and minor >= 0", forward-compatible), the review node fields, redaction, old-run behaviour, and a strong verification list (1.0.0/1.1.0/1.2.0 load, three transports, blocked review, attempt 2 and missing review are 404, diff confinement/symlink/hash/oversize, redaction). But it leaves choices open that the UI worker and browser seeds depend on: "artifact_id of your choice", "text/x-diff or text/plain", "404 with a code that says no review is recorded" (no code named). Its diff_artifact rule ("null when the file fails its checks, the reviews route still succeeds") forces the reviews route to open, bound-read and hash up to 32 MiB on every request and silently downgrades tampering to null. The C task's requirement_verbatim compares redacted quote to redacted task, which can false-link a literal "<path>" quote. The contract feeding the spec has gaps a faithful worker would inherit: checks[].kind omits typecheck/integration (policy schema allows six), check/scenario id use the route-ID pattern (rejects labels like test:unit), mode is z.enum(['interactive']), source_branch is required so runs without it get inputs:null. It says nothing about what happens when a review/inputs section is malformed. Meanwhile PR 10 bumps EXPORT_VERSION to "1.2.0" while main's adapter is z.literal('1.0.0'): every run recorded after merging PR 10 is RUN_STORAGE_INVALID in the viewer until B's feature run merges; disclosed at docs/HANDOFF_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md:76-77 but self-inflicted by shipping the producer bump before the consumer. Two workers given this spec would produce broadly equivalent but not interchangeable code.
data.pr11: Shipped adapter code of high quality, consistent with main's style (ProjectApiError codes, readBounded/openDirectory/withRunsRoot reuse, JSDoc one-liners, routes registered via the paths map so the 405 loop and HEAD cover them). Export acceptance is an explicit enum of 1.0.0/1.1.0/1.2.0 (server/projects.ts:44) with review/inputs optional-or-null and strictly validated (:73-90, :123-142), and values.review is never mined. Redaction is materially improved (:57): my probe shows main leaves "[/home/u/x]", "|/home/u/x|", "<~/x/y>", "*~/a/b*" and "file:///home/..." unredacted while PR 11 redacts all of them, with no regression on URLs, relative paths or "2/3". review.diff is registered only under the literal path "review.diff" (:89), served via the existing artifact route with the same no-follow bounded read, an added size check (:651), text/plain + nosniff + CSP sandbox, and the test fixture deliberately embeds "<script>alert(1)</script>". requirement_found_in matches raw quote against raw task/prompt and additionally requires the redacted quote to survive in the served (64 KiB-bounded) text (:397-406); nothing is inferred. Absent sections are 404 REVIEW_NOT_FOUND/INPUTS_NOT_FOUND (:592-605), malformed ones are RUN_STORAGE_INVALID naming only the run. Tests (30, up from 22) assert no root path and no /home|/tmp|/var in every error body, snapshot the run tree to prove reads never write, cover 405/HEAD on the new routes and a 22-case malformed-section matrix. Weaknesses are modest: exact-version enum plus eager section validation means one 1.3.0 or one bad receipt field in one run makes the whole workflow list 500 (pre-existing pattern, larger surface now); checks[].command and setup[].command pass through unredacted by design; validateReviewResult runs three times per review request; native_started_at above 8.64e15 ms throws RangeError into the generic 500 path; the feature README still says "not an implementation" while the same PR ships it. Its own adapter-task.md matches the shipped code line for line and is precise enough to reproduce it.
data.ranking_reason: PR 11 is the only PR with adapter code and the code is careful, well-tested and stylistically consistent with main; on the security points that matter here (redaction, artifact registry checks, bounded reads, path-free errors, never guessing a match) it is verifiably better than what main has today. PR 10's specification is competent and its verification list is good, but it leaves load-bearing details open, prescribes a heavier diff_artifact design, inherits contract gaps, and ships an export bump that breaks the viewer for new runs until the future adapter lands. PR 9 has nothing on this dimension, which is correct for slice A, so it ranks last by definition rather than by fault.

findings.title: Redaction regex genuinely closes Markdown-punctuation and file:// gaps
findings.detail: PR 11 replaces main's lookbehind allow-list with a negative lookbehind on path characters plus an explicit file:// branch. A scratch probe shows main leaves paths inside [], ||, <>, ** and file:/// unredacted while PR 11 redacts all of them, and neither regex touches https URLs, relative paths, './x', '../x' or '2/3'. The test at server/projects.test.ts:1197 pins every spelling.
findings.evidence: server/projects.ts:57 `text.replace(/(?:file:\/\/(?=\/)|(?<![A-Za-z0-9._@~+/-]))(?:~|\/[A-Za-z0-9._@~+-]+)(?:\/[A-Za-z0-9._@~+-]*)+/g, '<path>')`. Probe (node redact.mjs): input `see [/home/u/x](/home/u/x) and |/home/u/x| and <~/x/y> *~/a/b*` -> main: `see [/home/u/x](<path>) and |/home/u/x| and <~/x/y> *~/a/b*`; ultra: `see [<path>](<path>) and |<path>| and <<path>> *<path>*`. `file:///home/u/repo/x.ts` -> main unchanged, ultra `<path>`. `https://example.com/a/b`, `src/projects/api.ts`, `../up/x`, `2/3` unchanged in both.

findings.title: review.diff artifact registration is pinned, hash-and-size checked and served with safe headers
findings.detail: The export's diff registration only validates with path literally 'review.diff' (traversal is rejected at schema level, tests review-diff-path / review-diff-traversal), the artifact id is derived from the registered hash, the file is read through the existing no-follow bounded reader under artifactByteLimit, and the served bytes must match both registered sha256 and byte count. Content type is text/plain with nosniff and CSP sandbox; the fixture embeds a script tag to prove it is inert. Untrusted packets do not block the review diff and a tampered registration surfaces as ARTIFACT_HASH_MISMATCH rather than a silently null link.
findings.evidence: server/projects.ts:89 `diff: z.strictObject({ path: z.literal(REVIEW_DIFF_FILE), sha256: hex64, bytes: ... })`; :617 `registered.push({ components: [REVIEW_DIFF_FILE], kind: 'patch', ... bytes: run.reviewDiff.bytes })`; :651 `if ((artifact.bytes !== null && bytes.length !== artifact.bytes) || sha256(bytes) !== artifact.sha256)`. Test server/projects.test.ts:979-1024 covers served/tampered/shorter/missing/symlinked-outside/oversize/none with `assert.equal(served.headers['content-type'], 'text/plain; charset=utf-8')`, nosniff, `default-src 'none'; sandbox`, and `assert.ok(!linked.body.includes('top secret'))`.

findings.title: requirement_found_in never guesses and is guarded against the served-text cut
findings.detail: A lane is linked only when the raw quote is a substring of the raw task (or prompt when the task is empty) AND the redacted quote survives in the bounded served text, so a link can never point at text the viewer cannot show. A quote written with the literal '<path>' marker does not match raw text; a paraphrase does not match; a null requirement yields []. The contract's cross-field validator additionally rejects links without a quote and duplicate lanes.
findings.evidence: server/projects.ts:397-406 `return text.includes(requirement) && boundedText(text).text.includes(served)`. Tests: server/projects.test.ts:932-960 asserts `requirement_found_in` = `[['ui'], [], [], ['ui'], [], ['adapter'], []]` for verbatim / paraphrase / none / path-in-quote / '<path>'-literal / both / legacy-null; :1197-1234 asserts a quote verbatim in the raw task but past the 64 KiB cut yields `[]`.

findings.title: Test file is stronger than main's on negative paths and leak checks
findings.detail: Every error assertion routes through assertError, which checks the body shape, that the temp root never appears, and that the message matches no /home|/tmp|/var path. The read-only test snapshots the run tree before and after hitting all routes including the new ones, checks 405+Allow for five methods and HEAD 200. The malformed-section test enumerates 22 mutations (unknown version, wrong types, extra keys carrying absolute paths, absolute/traversal owned_paths, foreign lane, duplicate check ids, browser without scenarios, unconfirmed stop with a time) and asserts the run list names only the run directory. Fixtures mirror real receipts (offset +00:00 timestamps, epoch-ms native_started_at) as found in the live run's ui.interactive.json.
findings.evidence: server/projects.test.ts:287-295 assertError; :396-418 read-only/405/HEAD over `url('alpha','main','run-002','/reviews/1')`, `/inputs` and `/artifacts/patch-review-<sha12>`; :1141-1195 malformed matrix with `assert.ok(!list.body.includes('/home/someone') && !list.body.includes('/etc/passwd'))`; :208-212 fixture `launch_requested_at: '2026-03-01T10:00:00.331982+00:00', native_started_at: Date.parse(...)` matching ~/.local/state/.../project-workflows-001/ui.interactive.json (`"launch_requested_at": "2026-09-21T14:33:25.331982+00:00", "native_started_at": 1790001207771`).

findings.title: Adapter code follows main's conventions and its adapter-task.md matches the shipped code
findings.detail: New routes are added to the paths map so the existing 405 loop and Fastify HEAD handling cover them; conform() is reused; errors are ProjectApiError with upper-snake codes; invalidRun() redacts issue text; helper functions carry the same one-line JSDoc style. PR 11's features/*/adapter-task.md names the exact version set, route, error codes, artifact id format, content type, headers, truncation limit and marker string, timestamp normalisation and launch_node_id rule, and each item corresponds to shipped code.
findings.evidence: server/projectRoutes.ts:110-111 paths.review/paths.inputs; :167-180 `conform(schemas.reviewResult, crossChecked(() => validateReviewResult(review), log), log)`. features/run-inputs/adapter-task.md:37 "truncated to 65536 characters with the marker `\n\n[… truncated by the viewer API: N more characters]`" matches server/projects.ts:378-385; features/review-result/adapter-task.md:14 "artifact id `patch-review-<first 12 hex of sha256>` ... `text/plain; charset=utf-8` inline" matches :366-368 and CONTENT_TYPES.patch.

findings.title: Exact-version enum plus eager section validation lets one run poison the whole workflow list
findings.detail: exportSchema.version is z.enum(['1.0.0','1.1.0','1.2.0']) and review/inputs are projected eagerly inside projectRun, which listRuns calls for every run. One run exported at 1.2.1/1.3.0, or one receipt field the strict section schema rejects (e.g. a policy check kind outside the enum, a non-UTC timestamp string, an unexpected key), makes GET .../runs a 500 for the entire workflow. This is main's pre-existing pattern for the core export, but the validated surface grew from about a dozen fields to roughly sixty optional-receipt fields. PR 10's spec asks for 'major 1 and minor >= 0', which is more forward-compatible. The test explicitly pins the whole-list failure.
findings.evidence: server/projects.ts:44 `const EXPORT_VERSIONS = ['1.0.0', '1.1.0', '1.2.0'] as const`; :693 `// Sections are projected eagerly so a contradictory review or assignment fails the run as a whole`; server/projects.test.ts:1163 case `{ ...base, runId: 'unknown-version', version: '1.3.0', ... }` and :1187-1188 `const list = await get(app, url('alpha', 'main')); assertError(list, 500, 'RUN_STORAGE_INVALID', root)`. Contrast features/review-result/adapter-task.md (PR 10):11 "Accept run-state.json exports whose version has major 1 and minor >= 0 (1.0.0, 1.1.0, 1.2.0, later 1.2.x)".

findings.title: checks[].command and setup[].command are served unredacted by design
findings.detail: Task, prompt, summaries, assumptions, finding messages and quotes all pass through redactPaths, but the joined argv commands do not, so an absolute interpreter or config path in a committed policy.json would reach the client. This is deliberate (the contract says command must equal the verifier's recorded command so a required check links to its execution) and consistent with main's projectWorkerResult, which also passes check commands through unredacted; the current policies contain no absolute paths. Worth a README note that policy commands are treated as operator-public.
findings.evidence: server/projects.ts:441 `id: check.id, kind: check.kind, command: check.command, ...`; :456 `setup: section.setup.map(step => ({ command: step.command, timeout_seconds: step.timeout_seconds }))`; contracts/projects/v1.ts (PR 11) "The approved argv joined exactly as the verifier records executed commands, so check IDs can be matched to executed checks". Probe: `python3 -c ... re.findall(r'"(/[^"]*)"', json.dumps(policy))` on the live policy.json -> `[]`.

findings.title: Oversized native_started_at reaches the generic 500 path instead of RUN_STORAGE_INVALID
findings.detail: The section schema accepts any non-negative integer for native_started_at, but new Date(n).toISOString() throws RangeError for n > 8.64e15, which escapes projectInputs, is not a ProjectApiError, and becomes 500 INTERNAL via the scope error handler. No path leaks (the message is fixed), so this is a wrong-code nit, not a security issue; a .max(8.64e15) on the schema or a try/catch would make it RUN_STORAGE_INVALID like every other malformed field.
findings.evidence: server/projects.ts:446 `native_started_at: worker.launch.native_started_at === null ? null : new Date(worker.launch.native_started_at).toISOString()`; :112 `native_started_at: z.number().int().nonnegative().nullable()`. Probe: `try { new Date(1e20).toISOString() } catch (e) { ... }` -> `big epoch -> RangeError Invalid time value`.

findings.title: Review payload is validated three times per request and redaction is recomputed per lane per finding
findings.detail: projectRun already calls validateReviewResult (and validateRunInputs) when loading the run; the route then wraps the same object in crossChecked(validateReviewResult) and conform(schemas.reviewResult). Harmless but redundant. Separately, lanesQuoting calls boundedText(text) (a full redaction pass over up to 256 KiB of task text) for each finding x lane, and because sections are projected eagerly this runs for every run on every list request. Bounded and small today, but it compounds the existing per-request packet loading the live reviewer already flagged.
findings.evidence: server/projects.ts:696-706 `inputs = validateRunInputs(projectInputs(...))` / `review = validateReviewResult(projectReview(...))`; server/projectRoutes.ts:167-174 `conform(schemas.reviewResult, crossChecked(() => validateReviewResult(review), log), log)`; server/projects.ts:400-405 `return WORKER_LANES.filter(lane => { ... return text.includes(requirement) && boundedText(text).text.includes(served) })`.

findings.title: Feature READMEs still describe the adapter as future worker work that the same PR ships
findings.detail: features/review-result/README.md and features/run-inputs/README.md say the directory is 'the committed assignment for the two workers ... not an implementation' and the adapter tasks open with 'Implement the backend side of slice B/C', while server/ in the same commit contains the implementation. The PRD status lines do record that the slices were implemented directly and that the feature directories 'exist for a later run', so this is stale wording rather than a misleading claim, but a worker launched from these tasks would re-implement shipped routes.
findings.evidence: features/review-result/README.md:3 "This directory is the committed assignment for the two workers of `docs/PRD_REVIEW_RESULT.md`, **not** an implementation."; features/review-result/adapter-task.md:3 "Implement the backend side of slice B ... on the existing Fastify server."; docs/PRD_REVIEW_RESULT.md (PR 11) "Status: Implemented 2026-09-21 on branch `ultra` directly in the checkout rather than as a feature run ...; the `review-result` feature directory and launch choice exist for a later run."; server/projects.ts:592 `async reviewResult(...)` shipped.

findings.title: Snapshot projection changes beyond the PRD B/C adapter deliverables
findings.detail: projectSnapshot now ignores non-status events when picking a node's last event and maps a new 'interrupted' event status to paused. Both are reasonable (a trailing 'stopped' note no longer masks the last status; an interrupted native review is unresolved, not pending) and tested, but neither is listed in the PRD adapter deliverables or the contract README's state-projection rules, and the first alters projection for existing runs whose last recorded event is a 'stopped' record.
findings.evidence: server/projects.ts:239 `interrupted: 'paused'`; :842 `if (EVENT_STATUS[event.status] !== undefined) lastEvent.set(node, event)` (main: `lastEvent.set(node, event)` unconditionally); test server/projects.test.ts:1241-1262. Live events.jsonl statuses include `stopped` (probe: `['approved','blocked','interactive','passed','running','stopped','succeeded']`).

findings.title: Deviates from PRD C wording (inputs: null) in favour of 404 INPUTS_NOT_FOUND, documented
findings.detail: PRD_RUN_INPUTS section 5 asks the adapter for 'inputs: null for runs without the section' and 'a verbatim match flag per finding'. PR 11 returns 404 INPUTS_NOT_FOUND and an array requirement_found_in of lanes instead. Both are defensible (the 404 keeps the payload strict and the UI maps the code to 'not recorded'; lanes handle worker=both without a second field) and the contract README records the 404 convention, but it is a deviation from the PRD's literal deliverable that PR 10's spec follows.
findings.evidence: docs/PRD_RUN_INPUTS.md (main) section 5: "`inputs: null` for runs without the section; requirement-quote lookup exposed as a verbatim match flag per finding"; server/projects.ts:603 `if (!run.inputs) throw new ProjectApiError(404, 'INPUTS_NOT_FOUND', ...)`; contracts/projects/README.md (PR 11) "A run whose export predates a section returns a 404 with code `REVIEW_NOT_FOUND` or `INPUTS_NOT_FOUND`"; features/run-inputs/adapter-task.md (PR 10):42 "`{ \"inputs\": RunInputs | null }` ... `null` when the section is absent or null".

findings.title: Adapter-task verification list is concrete and names the negative paths
findings.detail: The B task's verification paragraph enumerates exactly the cases a security-minded reviewer would want: all three export versions load, three transports, findings with and without worker/requirement, blocked review, attempt 2 and missing review are 404, diff confinement/symlink/hash-mismatch/oversize failures, redaction in messages and quotes, and existing tests passing without project configuration. It also fixes the version-acceptance rule (major 1, minor >= 0), pins ownership to server/ and config/projects.example.json, and carries the honesty clause about not claiming unexecuted tests. The C task adds truncation-marker passthrough and the true/false/null matrix for requirement_verbatim including both and none.
findings.evidence: features/review-result/adapter-task.md (PR 10):21 "export versions 1.0.0, 1.1.0 and 1.2.0 all load; a review section with native, print and manual transports; ... attempt 2 and missing review are 404; ... the diff artifact's confinement, symlink, hash-mismatch and oversize failures; path redaction in messages and quotes"; features/run-inputs/adapter-task.md (PR 10):49 "`requirement_verbatim` true, false and null cases including `both` and `none`, and the null case when inputs are missing; unknown run is 404".

findings.title: Spec leaves load-bearing choices open that the UI worker and seeds depend on
findings.detail: The B task says the artifact_id is 'of your choice', the content type is 'text/x-diff or text/plain', and the missing-review 404 uses 'a code that says no review is recorded' without naming it. The UI worker runs in parallel against the same spec and must mock the reviews route, seed candidate-mode runs and branch on the 404 code, so two workers could ship non-interlocking choices (e.g. UI expects REVIEW_NOT_FOUND, adapter emits NO_REVIEW). Compare PR 11's adapter task, which fixes `patch-review-<sha12>`, `text/plain; charset=utf-8`, `REVIEW_NOT_FOUND`, `INPUTS_NOT_FOUND` and the exact truncation marker.
findings.evidence: features/review-result/adapter-task.md (PR 10):12 "a run without a review section is 404 with a code that says no review is recorded"; :14 "(`artifact_id` of your choice, content type `text/x-diff` or `text/plain`, ...)". PR 11 features/review-result/adapter-task.md:12 "404 `REVIEW_NOT_FOUND` when the run has no review section or the attempt is not the recorded one"; :14 "artifact id `patch-review-<first 12 hex of sha256>` ... served `text/plain; charset=utf-8` inline".

findings.title: diff_artifact null-on-check-failure forces a full diff read on every reviews request and hides tampering
findings.detail: The spec requires diff_artifact to be null 'when the export has no diff or the file fails its checks (the reviews route still succeeds)'. To know whether the file fails its checks the reviews route must open, bound-read (up to 32 MiB) and hash review.diff on every call, and a hash mismatch or symlink is then reported as 'no diff' rather than as evidence tampering. The live run's review.diff is 289 KB, so the cost is real but bounded; the bigger issue is that a security signal (ARTIFACT_HASH_MISMATCH) is downgraded to an absence. PR 11 instead links by registry and lets the artifact route fail loudly (test 'tampered' asserts the link is present and the artifact route returns ARTIFACT_HASH_MISMATCH).
findings.evidence: features/review-result/adapter-task.md (PR 10):14 "`diff_artifact` is `null` when the export has no diff or the file fails its checks (the reviews route still succeeds)". Live run: `-rw-rw-r-- 1 agentops agentops 289187 Sep 21 15:36 review.diff`. PR 11 server/projects.test.ts:1019-1021 `const tampered = validateReviewResult(...); assert.equal(tampered.diff!.artifact_id, \`patch-review-${'e'.repeat(12)}\`)` with :1009 `assertError(await artifact('tampered', ...), 500, 'ARTIFACT_HASH_MISMATCH', root)`.

findings.title: Contract feeding the spec has enum and pattern gaps a faithful worker would inherit
findings.detail: PR 10's runInputs contract allows checks[].kind of only build/unit/browser/contract while the committed policy schema allows six kinds (typecheck, integration too); check and scenario ids use the 128-char route-ID pattern, which rejects free-form policy labels (e.g. test:unit, 'review verdict / narrow'); mode is z.enum(['interactive']) (a single-value enum copied from plan.mode); source_branch is non-nullable and export_inputs returns None when the plan lacks it, so such runs get inputs: null with no way to show even the task text. A worker implementing the spec against this contract would make the inputs route a 500 RESPONSE_INVALID for any policy using the other two kinds or a colon in a check id. PR 11's contract matches the six kinds and accepts free-form labels (tested).
findings.evidence: contracts/projects/v1.ts (PR 10) `kind: z.enum(['build', 'unit', 'browser', 'contract'])`, `id: id`, `scenarios: z.array(z.strictObject({ id: id, ... }))`, `mode: z.enum(['interactive'])`, `source_branch: z.string().min(1)`; workflow/export_state.py (PR 10) `if policy is None or "source_branch" not in plan: return None`. Probe on main: contracts/workflow/verification.schema.json enums -> `['build','typecheck','unit','integration','contract','browser']`, check id `{'type': 'string', 'minLength': 1}`. PR 11 contracts/projects/contract.test.ts `older.workers[0].checks[0].id = 'test:unit'` validates.

findings.title: requirement_verbatim compares redacted quote to redacted task, which can false-link a literal <path> quote
findings.detail: The C task says the flag is true 'when the redacted quote is a verbatim substring of the redacted task text'. A reviewer who writes the quote with the marker '<path>' (copying it from the viewer) would then match any task that contains a redacted absolute path at that position, which is a small guess by construction. PR 11 matches raw against raw and only then checks the redacted quote survives in the served text, and tests the '<path>'-literal case yields no link.
findings.evidence: features/run-inputs/adapter-task.md (PR 10):44 "`true` when the redacted quote is a verbatim substring of the redacted task text of the named worker"; features/run-inputs/README.md (PR 10) "the verbatim lookup compares redacted quote to redacted task". PR 11 server/projects.test.ts:943 `finding({ message: 'A redacted spelling is not the raw text.', worker: 'ui', requirement: 'Write the harness to <path> before anything else.' })` -> `[]`.

findings.title: Export bumped to 1.2.0 while the shipped adapter still requires exactly 1.0.0
findings.detail: PR 10 changes EXPORT_VERSION to '1.2.0' in workflow/export_state.py but does not touch server/projects.ts, where exportSchema.version is z.literal('1.0.0'). Every run recorded after PR 10 merges is RUN_STORAGE_INVALID in the viewer, and because listRuns projects every run, one such run makes the whole workflow list a 500 until slice B's feature run lands its adapter. The handoff discloses this honestly and defers `workflow export` on the live run for the same reason, but it is a self-inflicted interim breakage from shipping the producer bump ahead of the consumer; keeping the producer at 1.0.0 (as PR 9 does) or landing the two-line version-acceptance change (as PR 11 does) would have avoided it.
findings.evidence: workflow/export_state.py (PR 10) `EXPORT_VERSION = "1.2.0"` and `value = {"version": EXPORT_VERSION, ...}`; server/projects.ts on main :37 `const EXPORT_VERSION = '1.0.0'` / :52 `version: z.literal(EXPORT_VERSION)` (unchanged in PR 10: `git diff 61e4752..a1fab98 --stat` lists no server/ file); docs/HANDOFF_REVIEW_VISIBILITY.md (PR 10):76-77 "the adapter on `main` accepts export version 1.0.0 only, so re-exporting the live run before slice B's adapter merges would break the viewer ... new runs export at version 1.2.0, which the current adapter rejects for that run's listing".

findings.title: Spec is silent on malformed review/inputs sections
findings.detail: Neither PR 10 adapter task says what the adapter does when the review or inputs section is present but fails validation (500 for the run only, 500 for the workflow list, or serve the run without the section). Given main's eager-projection pattern this is the highest-blast-radius decision the worker will make, and PR 11's task states it explicitly ('RUN_STORAGE_INVALID naming the run but never a path') and tests it.
findings.evidence: features/review-result/adapter-task.md (PR 10):11-17 covers absent/null sections and unknown top-level keys only; PR 11 features/review-result/adapter-task.md:11 "A violation is `RUN_STORAGE_INVALID` naming the run but never a path. Never trust `values.review`."

findings.title: No adapter work, and none needed: producer left at 1.0.0 so the viewer is unaffected
findings.detail: PR 9 confines itself to slice A and leaves workflow/export_state.py at version 1.0.0, so main's z.literal('1.0.0') adapter keeps loading every new run and the live project-workflows-001 export continues to validate. There is nothing to review on this dimension and nothing misleading about that; it is the restraint the umbrella PRD asked for.
findings.evidence: pr9.diff touches no server/ or workflow/export_state.py file (task-stated file set: 21 files, slice A only); server/projects.ts on main :37 `const EXPORT_VERSION = '1.0.0'`; ~/.local/state/md-manager-workflows/project-workflows/project-workflows-001/run-state.json `version` = `1.0.0` (probe output `1.0.0 2026-09-21T14:33:23.528543Z 2026-09-21T15:52:04.675731Z`).

content.content: Structured output provided successfully
